findings.title: Comment contradicts the heading expectation it sits next to
findings.message: The replacement comment claims the composite disclosure header “retains Core shadow styling,” yet the very next assertion still expects the heading’s disabled-state height to be 6px smaller than normal — exactly the “drops shadow margins” shrinkage the deleted comment described. Either the comment misdescribes the new behavior or the first expectation is stale; a reader cannot tell which of the two is authoritative for `heading`.
findings.suggestion: Reconcile the comment with the first expectation: either explain what the remaining 6px heading shrink comes from (e.g. “the heading button still drops its shadow margins when disabled; managed fields and action buttons no longer do”) or, if the header is meant to keep full decoration, change the first expected shrink to 0.

findings.title: `afterY-6` duplicates the sum of the per-section shrink literals
findings.message: The expected displacement of `section-after` is hand-maintained as a magic number (-14 before, -6 now) that must always equal the sum of the three per-section shrinks (6+2+6=14 previously, 6+0+0=6 now). If a future edit changes one shrink value but forgets the displacement literal, the test fails confusingly (“disabled section layout”) instead of pointing at the real mismatch.
